name: Mount Baldy
summary: Apache County, AZ lookout on Mount Baldy (Dzil Ligai) on the Fort Apache Reservation; staffed 1914-1918, abandoned 1958, rubble by 2004.
status_note: FFLA lists it gone; a June 1, 2004 photo shows only a pile of rubble; the survey datasheet says the building was abandoned in 1958
agency: White Mountain Apache Tribe (Fort Apache Indian Reservation); the reservation boundary runs part way up the eastern slope, where the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests begin

access.note: On the Fort Apache Indian Reservation. The tribe has designated the area around the sacred mountain as tribal wilderness, with activities that would damage it off-limits. No source describes a permit process for the lookout site.

events.note: The Supervisor could not station a lookout on the mountain because of snow near the summit; a lookout man was now on this point (St. Johns Herald and Apache News, May 28, 1914, reprinted by Forest Lookouts)

Forestry Department engaged Miss Crosby to take charge of the lookout station at the top for the season (St. Johns Observer item, reprinted by Forest Lookouts) The item names only Mt. Baldy or Old Baldy, so the link to this mountain rests on its St. Johns origin.
Survey datasheet says the building was abandoned in 1958
Photo taken June 1, 2004 shows only a pile of rubble; the survey benchmark is still there
